title: A Shrew Smells Underwater by Blowing Bubbles and Sucking Them Back
subject: American water shrew

scenes.text: Nothing can smell underwater. This shrew does.
The American water shrew. Smaller than a mouse, it hunts in cold streams at night, diving for insects and small fish.
A high-speed camera at Vanderbilt University caught what it does down there. It blows a bubble onto whatever it is checking.
Then it sucks the same bubble back in, carrying the scent. Five to ten times a second.
Scientists laid scented trails underwater, and the shrew followed them. The bubbles were its nose.
It attacks what it finds in about a twentieth of a second, faster than a blink. A nose that works underwater, one bubble at a time.

description:
The American water shrew can smell underwater: it blows air bubbles onto objects and re-inhales them, carrying scent back to its nose, five to ten times a second.
Vanderbilt University biologist Kenneth Catania filmed the behaviour with high-speed video in 2006, in star-nosed moles and water shrews, and showed the animals could follow underwater scent trails. Later work showed water shrews strike at prey within about 50 milliseconds.
Which animal sense would you most like to have?
first_comment: It also has to eat about its own body weight every day or it starves. Which animal sense would you steal if you could?
